page: Google Cloud Platform m1-ultramem-40 is a specialized memory-optimized instance designed for enterprise applications that demand substantial memory capacities. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 40 dedicated vCPUs spanning 20 physical Intel Xeon processor cores running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The system provides an expansive memory allocation of 961 GB, translating to approximately 24.02 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 55 MB of L3 cache, standard AVX vector support, and AES cryptographic instructions. The instance does not include GPU acceleration or local ephemeral storage, meaning all persistent data relies on external cloud storage volumes.

Benchmark evaluations emphasize a profile skewed toward parallel execution rather than per-core speed. Single-core results on stress-ng and Geekbench register in the lower tiers, reflecting the 2.2 GHz operating frequency and older microarchitecture. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads demonstrate stable performance, registering 20,102.36 on stress-ng multi-core and 7,502.0 on Geekbench multi-core. In memory subsystems, the server records uncached read bandwidth of 61.46 GB/s and cached small-block throughput exceeding 1,520 GB/s. High-throughput data access is corroborated by Redis performance yielding 21.2 million operations per second and steady database transaction testing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, m1-ultramem-40 trades compute efficiency for exceptional memory density. Workloads requiring compute-heavy vector processing or advanced instruction extensions such as AVX-512 will encounter hardware bottlenecks on this platform. However, for organizations managing footprint-heavy datasets that must reside entirely in memory, consolidating onto a single large-memory node avoids distributed synchronization overhead. The server is suited for in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, enterprise ERP platforms, and memory-intensive business analytics.
description: Google Cloud Platform m1-ultramem-40 is a memory-optimized server configuration tailored for extreme memory-density applications. It features 40 dedicated vCPUs derived from 20 physical Intel Xeon cores clocked at 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, coupled with a massive 961 GB of RAM, delivering over 24 GB of memory per core. The instance provides no bundled local storage and includes no GPU accelerators, delegating persistent storage entirely to network-attached disks. Benchmark metrics indicate moderate multi-core processing throughput alongside lower single-core execution speed, consistent with older-generation Xeon architectures with conservative clock rates. Its memory bandwidth achieves 61.46 GB/s on uncached reads, while Redis operations reach 21.2 million operations per second. This instance represents a specialized resource profile where high RAM capacity is prioritized over compute velocity. Google Cloud Platform m1-ultramem-40 is engineered primarily for in-memory databases, large-scale caching systems, SAP HANA deployments, and memory-bound enterprise data analytics workloads.
